communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Steven Catron (Burlington Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Steven Catron (6303-1830)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to the Aberdeen School District, its legal counsel, its board of directors, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, voucher approvals, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee, specifically including but not limited to Warrant No. 837374 approved on or around December 17, 2024.
3. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 4, 2022, through June 30, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks, settlement agreements, and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:
The District is advised that, per Washington law (Progressive Animal Welfare Soc. v. University of Wash.), attorney billing records for public payment are subject to disclosure. Only specific, narrow redactions (e.g., student names under FERPA) are permitted, as blanket privilege claims are invalid under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:
A response is expected within five business days as per RCW 42.56.520. The records, requested for non-commercial purposes, should be provided electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: Zero Authorization: DDOT Executive Dispatch Logs and Right-of-Entry Records for Urban Forestry Trespass
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO: sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov
CC:  earl.eutsler@dc.gov, frank.seales@dc.gov, ian.maggard@dc.gov, neelima.ghanta@dc.gov, richard.kenney@dc.gov, aaron.horton@dc.gov, pmendelson@dccouncil.gov, callen@dccouncil.gov, twhite@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com

SUBJECT: FOIA Request: Dispatch Logs, Right-of-Entry Clearances, and Executive Authorizations for August 17, 2026, UFD Site Visit (1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the Designated Freedom of Information Act Officer:

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am formally requesting complete, native-format records concerning the administrative authorization, dispatch logs, and internal dissemination of photographs regarding the Urban Forestry Division (UFD) site visit to my private property at 1490 Morris Rd SE on August 17, 2026.

PROCESSING CLARIFICATION:
This request is explicitly distinct from, and does not duplicate, my prior requests (including R012880-082026). Previous filings sought historical (2022–present) GPS metadata, general infrastructure plans, and the raw field notes of the responding forester. This current request strictly demands the executive chain-of-command approvals, dispatch tickets, Right-of-Entry/Consent logs, and internal communications that authorized the August 17, 2026 trespass and subsequent dissemination of site photographs.

LEGAL CONTEXT & STATUTORY BASIS:
District of Columbia standard operating procedures and municipal law (including D.C. Official Code § 22-3302 regarding Unlawful Entry) dictate that government personnel do not have a blanket right to enter private residential curtilage without a warrant, exigent life-saving circumstances, or explicit homeowner consent. In 2022 (under Work Order wo1075126), DDOT established a protocol of officially emailing and requesting my permission prior to entering the adjacent paper alley/property boundary. On August 17, 2026, that legal protocol was entirely abandoned. 

Please provide copies of the following specific records:

1. DISPATCH LOGS AND WORK ORDERS:
The complete Cityworks, Salesforce, or internal dispatch ticket/work order that directed an Urban Forestry Division official to report to 1490 Morris Rd SE on or around August 17, 2026. This must include the name of the authorizing supervisor or executive who generated the deployment.

2. RIGHT-OF-ENTRY / HOMEOWNER CONSENT DOCUMENTATION:
All signed consent forms, logged phone call transcripts, email clearances, or administrative liability waivers that legally authorized the UFD official to physically cross the private property boundary of 1490 Morris Rd SE on August 17, 2026. If the responding official self-dispatched, please provide the UFD policy permitting self-authorization onto private property without homeowner coordination.

3. EXECUTIVE AUTHORIZATION AND COMMUNICATIONS (AUG 14 - AUG 20, 2026):
All emails, SMS/text messages, and Microsoft Teams chats generated between August 14, 2026, and August 20, 2026, involving Director Sharon Kershbaum, Earl Eutsler, and Branch Chief Duff McCully regarding the authorization of this specific site visit and the internal reporting of the 25-foot landslide.

4. TRANSMITTAL AND METADATA OF THE SIX (6) PHOTOGRAPHS:
The internal routing communications and native unstripped metadata of the six (6) photographs taken during the unannounced August 17, 2026 visit. Director Kershbaum subsequently emailed these specific photographs to me across multiple messages, citing file size restrictions. I am requesting the internal emails showing exactly who transmitted these six photos to Director Kershbaum's inbox and the exact time they were received.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST: 
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search and reproduction fees. Disclosure of these records is in the primary public interest, directly informing District residents, the D.C. Council, and investigative media at WUSA9 concerning procedural malfeasance, potential municipal trespass, and the executive handling of an active life-safety hazard. Please process this request electronically and provide all files in their original, native formats with all embedded metadata (including EXIF data, timestamps, and application histories) fully intact. If any records or portions of records are withheld or redacted, you must provide an itemized Vaughn Index justifying each specific deletion by reference to the applicable statutory exemption under D.C. Official Code § 2-534, along with a factual description of how disclosure would harm the protected interest.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

title: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (El Segundo Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (El Segundo Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We are working on an article focused on California police departments sharing local data with federal authorities, including ICE via LexisNexis. We identified your agency as part of a South Bay Regional Police Consortium that contracted with LexisNexis for AVCC in or around 2020. This request focuses on data your agency shares with LexisNexis, and interfaces that exist with your agency's RMS/CAD/JMS and LexisNexis's systems, including Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), CommunityCrimeMap.com, or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx)

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]
4) Occasionally we have found consortiums who have negotiated to only share local data with other consortium members, not the 2,400 AVCC federal and local LE subscribers. If you have documentation that your data is only shared locally, please share it. Otherwise you may state there are no responsive documents to item 4. 

We welcome (but do not expect or request) any comments you have about the sharing of local police data with federal authorities via LexisNexis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

title: Matter Concerning Case Referral / Declination: Laura Michelle Aufleger (Payne County District Attorney Referral)

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Matter Concerning Case Referral / Declination: Laura Michelle Aufleger (Payne County District Attorney Referral)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Open Records Officer / Records Custodian

Office of the Attorney General of Oklahoma

313 NE 21st Street

Oklahoma City, OK 73105
Submitted via Email: openrecordsrequest@oag.ok.gov / opengov@oag.ok.gov
Attention: Public Access Counselor / AAG Tony Sykes

RE: URGENT OKLAHOMA OPEN RECORDS ACT REQUEST

Matter Concerning Case Referral / Declination: Laura Michelle Aufleger (Payne County District Attorney Referral)

(Pursuant to 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq.)

Dear Records Custodian and Public Access Counselor Tony Sykes:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq., and in light of Attorney General Gentner Drummond’s explicit commitment to government transparency and public accountability, I hereby submit this formal request for public records maintained by the Office of the Oklahoma Attorney General.

This request directly concerns any referral, communication, review, conflict of interest disclosure, or declination of prosecution sent from the Payne County District Attorney’s Office (District 9) to the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office regarding Laura Michelle Aufleger (Case Number: OHP26-002728).

According to Oklahoma Highway Patrol Incident/Offense Report OHP26-002728 and court filings, Laura Michelle Aufleger was arrested on February 13, 2026 at approximately 21:41 hours on the following charges:

*Operate Vehicle While Under The Influence Of Alcohol (Aggravated DUI -- BAC OF 0.15 Or More) (FELONY) — 47 O.S. § 11-902.D.1 (Breath-Alcohol Analysis result recorded as 0.21 BrAC).

*Leaving Scene of Accident Resulting in Damage to Fixtures, Fences or Any Other Property Adjacent to Highway — 47 O.S. § 10-106.

*Child Endangerment (DUI or APC While Transporting Child) (FELONY) — 21 O.S. § 852.1.A.4.


Serious public concerns exist regarding political influence, financial donations to campaigns, and community standing within Payne County, alongside potential reluctance to prosecute these multiple felony charges. Furthermore, numerous messages left with Constituent Services regarding this matter have gone unacknowledged and unreturned. I also reached out to Assistant Attorney General Tony Sykes for assistance in this matter today. Failing to address inquiries regarding potential conflict-of-interest referrals contradicts basic principles of open government and public transparency.

1. Requested Records

Please provide all electronic and physical records created, received, or maintained by the Office of the Attorney General from February 13, 2026 to the present regarding Laura Michelle Aufleger, including:

1. Referrals & Recusals: All referral letters, emails, memorandums, or conflict-of-interest recusal notices from the Payne County District Attorney’s Office transferring, requesting assistance with, or referring the investigation/prosecution of Laura Michelle Aufleger (Case Number: OHP26-002728) to the Attorney General’s Office.

2. Case Intake & Declination Files: All intake logs, legal review notes, case summaries, declination-to-prosecute letters, charging decisions, and internal communications regarding the disposition or review of Laura Michelle Aufleger's arrest.

3. Internal & External Communications:  All emails, text messages, phone logs, and written correspondence between the OAG (including Constituent Services, Executive Staff, and AAG Tony Sykes) and the Payne County District Attorney’s Office concerning Laura Michelle Aufleger.

4. Campaign Contribution & Conflict Records: All internal conflict analysis, recusal logs, or ethics reviews examining potential conflicts of interest related to campaign contributions, donations, or community influence involving Laura Michelle Aufleger, OnCue, or associated entities and donors.

5. Constituent Communication Logs All constituent intake logs, call transcripts, voicemails, phone logs, and email records documenting my unreturned messages left with Constituent Services and my outreach to AAG Tony Sykes regarding this matter.

---

2. Statutory Authority & Presumption of Openness

Under Oklahoma law, public records are presumptively open for public inspection. Pursuant to 51 O.S. § 24A.5, public bodies exist to serve the public, and access to records shall not be unreasonably delayed or withheld. Any statutory doubts regarding disclosure must be resolved in favor of openness.

---

3. Timely Response Requirement

Under 51 O.S. § 24A.5(5), public bodies are mandated to provide "prompt, reasonable access" to records. Given that previous inquiries to Constituent Services have gone completely unaddressed, prompt compliance with this statutory obligation is requested.

---

4. Fee Waiver Request (Public Interest & Media Exception)

Under 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4):

* Search/labor fees may only be assessed if a request is for a commercial purpose or causes excessive disruption.
* Requests made for news media, educational, or public interest purposes concerning government operations do not constitute a commercial purpose.

This request directly concerns public oversight, prosecutor accountability, and potential conflicts of interest in the handling of felony charges. As such, I request a full waiver of fees. If electronic copies (PDF) are provided via email, no reproduction costs are incurred. If fees are expected to exceed $15.00, please provide an itemized fee schedule prior to processing.

---

5. Statutory Penalties for Non-Compliance

Please be advised of the statutory enforcement mechanisms governing public records in Oklahoma:

*Criminal Penalties: Pursuant to 51 O.S. § 24A.17(A), any public official who willfully violates any provision of the Oklahoma Open Records Act is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to one (1) year in the county jail, a fine not exceeding $500.00, or both.

*Civil Remedies & Mandatory Fees: Pursuant to 51 O.S. § 24A.17(B), any person denied access to public records may file a civil suit for injunctive or declaratory relief. The prevailing party shall be awarded reasonable attorney fees.

---

6. Redaction & Segregability Requirement

Pursuant to 51 O.S. § 24A.5(2), if any portion of the requested records is asserted to be exempt or confidential, the OAG is required to redact only the exempt portion and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt material. If any document or portion thereof is withheld, please provide a written privilege log citing the specific statutory exemption relied upon.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

The Landrun Lowdown

title: 25 Years of Neglect: Civil Engineering, Stormwater Blueprints, and Landslide Records for Morris Road SE

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: 25 Years of Neglect: Civil Engineering, Stormwater Blueprints, and Landslide Records for Morris Road SE
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO:  ddot.foia@dc.gov

CC: sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov, richard.jackson2@dc.gov, brian.hanlon@dc.gov, earl.eutsler@dc.gov, pmendelson@dccouncil.gov, callen@dccouncil.gov, twhite@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com

SUBJECT: FOIA Request: 25-Year Civil Infrastructure, Stormwater As-Builts, Hunter Pl Alley Maintenance, and Special Tree Threat Records (1600-1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the Designated Freedom of Information Act Officers:

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am requesting complete, native-format public records concerning the civil infrastructure, stormwater conveyance, public space maintenance, and geotechnical evaluations along the corridor from 1600 Morris Rd SE down the hillside to 1490 Morris Rd SE, including the public paper alley connecting from Hunter Place SE.

PROCESSING CLARIFICATION:
This request is explicitly distinct from previous requests. While previous filings sought specific supervisory correspondence and administrative records, this request strictly demands the physical civil engineering blueprints, 25-year maintenance and inspection histories, and current infrastructure performance data for the hillside corridor.

LEGAL AND STATUTORY BASIS FOR INQUIRY:
The physical infrastructure along this corridor is actively failing, resulting in an unmitigated 25-foot slope failure and mass wasting event that directly compromises:
1. Special Trees protected under the Urban Forest Preservation Act of 2002 (D.C. Official Code § 8-651.04), which strictly regulates and penalizes the unauthorized injury, destabilization, or destruction of healthy trees with a circumference of 44 to 99.9 inches;
2. Stormwater Management and Soil Erosion Mandates under 21 DCMR Chapter 5 and the D.C. Water Pollution Control Act (D.C. Official Code § 8-103.01 et seq.); and
3. Public Space Safety and Right-of-Way Maintenance Obligations pursuant to 24 DCMR Chapter 1 and D.C. Official Code § 9-101.01 et seq.

Please provide copies of the following specific records:

1. STORMWATER MANAGEMENT (SWM) AS-BUILTS & PERMITTING:
All approved Stormwater Management Plans, As-Built Certifications (mandated under 21 DCMR § 500 et seq.), and drainage plats for all commercial, residential, institutional, or public developments along the 1600 block of Morris Rd SE and the crest of the hill from 2001 to the present.

2. GEOTECHNICAL AND SLOPE STABILITY ASSESSMENTS:
All geotechnical surveys, soil boring logs, hydrology flow studies, and slope stability calculations conducted by or submitted to DOEE, DDOT, or DOB regarding Square 5812 and the Morris Road SE hillside failure zone.

3. 25-YEAR PUBLIC SPACE & ALLEY MAINTENANCE RECORDS (HUNTER PL SE TO MORRIS RD SE):
All maintenance logs, clearing work orders, public space inspection reports, grading surveys, and repair records from 2001 to the present for the public paper alley situated immediately behind 1488 and 1490 Morris Rd SE extending toward Hunter Place SE.

4. RETAINING WALL AND DRAINAGE INFRASTRUCTURE AS-BUILTS:
All structural permits, architectural plans, and engineering as-builts for all retaining walls, catch basins, interceptor drains, French drains, and surface water diversions constructed within the 1600-1490 Morris Rd SE corridor.

5. ARBORICULTURAL CLOSEOUT REPORTS & SPECIAL TREE ASSESSMENTS:
All formal inspection reports, Tree Risk Assessment Qualification (TRAQ) field evaluations, and Work Order Closeout Notes detailing the site conditions, ground destabilization, and root health recorded during the historical tree removal under Work Order wo1075126 (May 2022), as well as any current assessments evaluating the acute structural failure threatening the two identified Special Trees (D.C. Code § 8-651.04) on the active 25-foot landslide slope.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search and reproduction fees. Disclosure of these public safety, civil infrastructure, and environmental enforcement records is in the primary public interest, directly informing District residents, the D.C. Council, and investigative media at WUSA9 concerning an active hazard along a public school student pedestrian walking route.

Please process this request electronically and provide all files in their original, native formats. If any records or portions of records are withheld or redacted, you must provide an itemized Vaughn Index justifying each specific deletion by reference to the applicable statutory exemption under D.C. Official Code § 2-534, along with a factual description of how disclosure would harm the protected interest.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

title: DDOT Dir Sharon Kershbaum Communictions & Site Assessment Records:  Morris Rd SE Landslide and Heritage Tree Certification (02/01/26-present)

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: DDOT Dir Sharon Kershbaum Communictions & Site Assessment Records:  Morris Rd SE Landslide and Heritage Tree Certification (02/01/26-present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officer
Subject: FOIA Request: Communications, Calendar, and GPS Records for Director Sharon Kershbaum (Morris Rd SE)

To the Designated FOIA Officer:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am requesting specific digital records, communications, and metadata pertaining to DDOT Director Sharon Kershbaum. 

Please provide the following records generated between February 1, 2026, and the present date:
1. All emails, Microsoft Teams messages, SMS/text messages, and internal memos sent or received by Director Sharon Kershbaum containing any of the following keywords: "Morris Road", "Morris Rd", "Fred Gamble", "landslide", "slope failure", "canal", "ditch", "cherry tree", "heritage tree", "WUSA9", or "Lionel Donovan".
2. Director Kershbaum’s complete calendar entries, meeting invites, and meeting notes referencing the aforementioned keywords or any inter-agency coordination regarding Morris Road SE.
3. GPS logs and tracking telemetry for any District-issued vehicle utilized by Director Kershbaum or her immediate executive detail, specifically checking for proximity to the 1400-1600 blocks of Morris Rd SE.
4. All digital metadata, including read-receipts and ticket routing history, associated with Director Kershbaum’s review of 311 service requests or constituent emails regarding the slope failure at Morris Rd SE.

Fee Waiver Request:
I request a waiver of all fees associated with this request pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b). Disclosure of this information is strictly in the public interest as it will shed light on the executive leadership's response—or lack thereof—to an active 25-foot landslide with a 6-foot vertical sheer drop threatening protected Special Trees and a heavily trafficked student walking route. Given that WUSA9 investigative reporters are actively involved in reviewing the District's handling of this hazard, the public has a vital interest in knowing how agency directors allocate resources and prioritize life-safety emergencies. 

As a community advocate pursuing government accountability, I have no commercial interest in these records. If this fee waiver is denied, please provide a detailed statutory justification. If any records are redacted, please cite the specific FOIA exemptions applied.

Regards,

Fred Gamble Jr.
Ward 8 Resident & Community Advocate

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

Joey Scott

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Audit - National Lookups
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

On March 9th, your agency issued a press release about the use of Flock Safety cameras by federal agencies. Please provide the following information relating to your Flock Safety system: 

1) Please provide any internal audits, reports, or memos written about the audit your agency conducted after finding out the about the "National Lookup" configuration issue in Flock Safety. 

2) Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

3) Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

4) A list of network share settings that include:
 - 4a. Flock networks shared with me
 - 4b. Networks that I’m sharing

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine readable format. For example, please provide csv or spreadsheet files where applicable. Please do not redirect me to your transparency portal. I appreciate you taking the time to complete this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Alan J. Segal

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #PRR 26-54
communications.communication:
Dear Georgianna,

I write to appeal the redactions applied to the ALPR audit export produced in response to my request. The production redacts the entire Reason column, citing Government Code section 7923.600, and masks the Name, License Plate, Case #, and Filters columns with no cited authority at all. Both categories of redaction are improper.

The Reason column is not an investigatory record. In ACLU Foundation of Southern California v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032, the California Supreme Court held that ALPR data is not exempt under the investigatory records provision because plate scans are not targeted inquiries into particular crimes, and the fact that the database was searched does not change that analysis. An audit log documenting why department personnel queried a surveillance system is an accountability record about the agency's own conduct, not an investigative file. The exemption applies only where the prospect of enforcement proceedings is concrete and definite. Williams v. Superior Court (1993) 5 Cal.4th 337. A categorical redaction of every reason for every search, applied uniformly across the export, reflects no such record-by-record determination.

More fundamentally, the Legislature created this field for public oversight. Civil Code section 1798.90.52, enacted by SB 34, requires ALPR operators to maintain a record of access including the purpose for accessing the information. Withholding the purpose field defeats the accountability function the statute exists to serve. Agencies across California routinely release this field in response to identical requests.

The uncited redactions violate the CPRA on their face. Government Code section 7922.540 requires that any withholding be justified in writing with the applicable exemption identified. Section 7922.525(b) requires release of any reasonably segregable portion of a record. Masking columns via a system export setting, without citing any authority, satisfies neither. For each of the Name, Case #, and Filters columns, please identify the specific statutory exemption claimed and the persons responsible for the denial as section 7922.540 requires. Note that the names of peace officers are generally subject to disclosure. Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training v. Superior Court (2007) 42 Cal.4th 278. I do not contest redaction of the License Plate column.

The public interest here is clear. The Attorney General's Information Bulletin 2023-DLE-06 confirms that SB 34 prohibits sharing ALPR data with federal or out-of-state agencies, and the Attorney General has filed suit against a California city for violating that prohibition. Recent reporting has documented federal agencies querying local Flock systems in California, in some cases without the host agency's knowledge. The Reason column is the mechanism by which the public, and for that matter the Department itself, can verify that searches of Port Hueneme's system comply with state law. Results from other agencies list the "Org Name" as a CA-based agency, but the reason column makes it clear that the query is being run on behalf of a federal agency, or in one case in Illinois that I found, a local officer shared his Flock username and password with a federal agent. The search appeared local but was actually a DEA agent running a civil immigration related search using a local detective's login credentials. It was discovered due to the Reason column being reviewed by researchers following a public records request, such as this one. 

Please produce an unredacted Reason column. Exemptions under the CPRA must be narrowly construed. Cal. Const., art. I, § 3(b)(2). 

Sincerely,
Alan Segal

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Public Records Request — SanMateoCounty Generative AI Records
communications.communication:
Subject: Public Records Request — AI Chatbot Interaction Logs

April 9, 2026

Public Records Officer
San Mateo County
400 County Center
Redwood City, CA 94063

Dear Public Records Officer,

I am writing on behalf of a team of researchers and journalists from Stanford University, the University of Southern California, KNKX Public Radio and the New York Times. We are studying how government agencies are adopting and using AI tools in their daily work.

We are writing to request records related to San Mateo County's use of generative AI tools by county employees, including Innovaccer's Healthcare AI Platform.

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Cal. Gov. Code § 6253(c), we are requesting the following records:

1. All interaction logs from ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Claude, or any other generative AI chatbot tool — including prompts submitted by San Mateo County employees and responses generated by the AI — for the period from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. We request these records in their native electronic format where available (e.g., HTML exports, JSON, or CSV).

2. Any policies, guidelines, acceptable use policies, or training materials governing San Mateo County employee use of Innovaccer or other generative AI chatbot tools.

3. Any data retention or deletion policies applicable to AI chatbot interaction logs, including any schedules for automatic deletion of interaction data.

4. Administrative usage statistics showing number of users, sessions, and queries processed for any generative AI tools deployed to county employees.

We are seeking the substantive content of AI interactions for research purposes. We do not need personally identifying information of individual employees (such as names and email addresses).

San Mateo County Health selected Innovaccer's Healthcare AI Platform to improve delivery of public health services, providing clinicians with a comprehensive 360-degree view of patient data for approximately 165,000 active lives and 500,000 legacy lives. The platform incorporates Innovaccer's InNote solution into the county's EHR, enabling healthcare providers to search for patients across multiple EHR systems and review comprehensive medical records (see Business Wire, "San Mateo County Health Selects Innovaccer's Healthcare AI Platform to Improve Delivery of Public Health Services," July 24, 2024, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240724887877/en/; see also Innovaccer, "San Mateo County Health Selects Innovaccer's Healthcare AI Platform," https://innovaccer.com/news/san-mateo-county-selects-innovaccer-healthcare-ai-platform-improve-delivery-public-health-services). Innovaccer has since expanded its generative AI capabilities, introducing multiple copilots and agents for utilization management, clinical decision support, and care management (see Fierce Healthcare, "Innovaccer clinches $275M series F funding to build out AI, cloud capabilities," https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/health-tech/innovaccer-clinches-275m-series-f-funding-build-out-ai-cloud-capabilities).

We note that records of this type have been made available in response to public records requests in other jurisdictions. See Cascade PBS, WA City Officials Are Using ChatGPT to Write Government Documents (Aug. 2025), https://www.cascadepbs.org/news/2025/08/wa-city-officials-are-using-chatgpt-to-write-government-documents/; see also Texas State AI Usage — Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), MuckRock, https://www.muckrock.com/foi/texas-109/texas-state-ai-usage-texas-department-of-transportation-txdot-196227/#files.

The results of this research will be published in peer-reviewed academic venues and will contribute to public understanding of how public servants interact with AI systems. This request is made by an academic research institution for scholarly, non-commercial purposes; as such, we request a fee waiver or reduction. If a fee waiver is not granted, please inform me of estimated costs before proceeding. I am willing to pay fees up to $20.

I understand that this may be a novel type of records request and I am happy to answer any technical questions. Please feel free to contact me at the email address below.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Alexander Spangher
Postdoctoral Researcher
Stanford University
alexspan@stanford.edu

P.S. To facilitate your response, we note that Innovaccer's platform maintains interaction and query logs accessible through its administrative dashboard. For ChatGPT, conversation histories can be exported by individual users via Settings > Data Controls > Export Data. For Microsoft Copilot, interaction histories may be available through the Microsoft 365 admin console or the Purview compliance center. We are happy to provide additional technical guidance if that would be helpful.

P.P.S. The California Public Records Act defines "public records" to include any writing containing information relating to the conduct of the public's business, regardless of physical form or characteristics. Cal. Gov. Code § 7920.530. Governor Newsom's Executive Order N-12-23 (September 2023) directed state agencies to develop a generative AI framework, and the CalGovOps GenAI Policy Framework (2024) requires agencies to maintain inventories of AI/GenAI tools and document use cases. Consistent with this trend nationally, NARA has made clear that chats and other electronic messages used for agency business are likely government records. NARA Bulletin 2023-02 (Jan. 5, 2023), https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/bulletins/2023/2023-02.

The CPRA requires the agency to determine within 10 days of receipt whether the request, in whole or in part, seeks copies of disclosable public records in the possession of the agency and to promptly notify the person making the request of the determination and the reasons for the determination. Cal. Gov. Code § 7922.535(a). However, in unusual circumstances, the 10-day time limit may be extended by written notice by the head of the agency or designee, setting forth the reasons for the extension and the date on which a determination is expected to be provided. See Cal. Gov. Code § 7922.535(c).

We write you in our capacity as designee of the head of the agency to which your request was directed to notify you that unusual circumstances require an extension of the time in which to make the determination under Section 7922.535(a). Among the reasons for the extension are:

(1) The need to search for and collect the requested records from field facilities or other establishments that are separate from the office processing the request;

(2) The need to search for, collect, and appropriately examine a voluminous amount of separate and distinct records that are demanded in a single request; and

(3) The need for consultation with another agency having substantial interest in the determination of the request or among two or more components of the agency having substantial subject matter interest therein.

We expect to provide a determination under Section 7922.535(a) no later than May 10, 2026. Feel free to contact me with any questions.

communications.communication:
Hello Valerie and Sheila,

Thank you so much for your response! I'd love to schedule a phone call at the earliest convenience to discuss further. 

I acknowledge we filed a broad request. Just to give you some background of what we are trying to do, here, we are academic researchers and our primary goal is to assess:
  (1) how AI systems are being used in government
  (2) how academia can help improve these systems by (a) building benchmarks (b) outlining future methodological directions.
We hope these directions can mobilize research in academia to build tooling to better meet the needs of government employees and ultimately impact members of the public. Without data, though, it is hard to know where to start.

I do respectfully note that the CPRA's "reasonably describe an identifiable record" standard does not bar requests framed by category — California courts have long held a request is adequate so long as it enables the agency to identify and locate responsive records with reasonable effort, not that the requester must name specific documents. See California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court (1998) 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165–166; see also City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017)  2 Cal.5th 608, 627 (contemplating agencies conducting reasonable categorical searches of employee communications)

However, in order to make this request more tractable, we are more than willing to work cooperatively to narrow down the scope of records we request. We are seeking to obtain chat records from persons in the following roles:

  - Policy/regulatory staff
  - Communications/public affairs
  - Legal/counsel
  - Program/project management
  - Administrative/executive support
  - Technical/IT staff
  - Human resources
  - Budget/finance
  - Field/operations staff
  - Senior leadership

If it is constructive to filter down to chat logs from 10% or 5% of government employees currently in San Mateo, as long as they are evenly distributed across these roles, we would accept that constraint.

We are happy to work on our end to identify particular individuals or let you identify these individuals, whatever is preferred on your end. We are also very amenable to receiving anonymized data — we have no interest in identifying specific people. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Electronic copies of the following existing public records of the Third Judicial District Attorney's Office concerning Karpel Computer Systems, Inc. (PROSECUTORbyKarpel):

1. The executed agreement dated on or about June 30, 2023 for criminal case management software, data integration and configuration, technical and procedural workflow, support personnel, and cloud-based services (total contract price approximately $269,495.06), with all exhibits, statements of work, price schedules, and amendments.

2. The annual software support and maintenance agreements dated on or about September 1, 2023 and July 1, 2024 (approximately $55,875 each), with all exhibits and amendments.

3. The sole-source determination, written justification, and public posting associated with procurement number 40-25300-23-CP314, and any determination, solicitation, quotes, or price agreement relied upon for the 2023 agreement.

4. Any evaluation, scoring, or recommendation-of-award records for the 2023 agreement, and any implementation or acceptance records showing when the system went live.

I do not require the compilation of new records; existing records only. Electronic copies (PDF or native format) are requested. Please advise of any fees before incurring them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

cassy

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DOEE/DOB Internal Communications: Inspector Lawrence U. Omoregbe, Director Brian Hanlon, & Director Richard Jackson (1490 Morris Rd SE, S03-A8QMU) (Department Of Energy & Environment)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Subject: DOEE/DOB Internal Communications: Inspector Lawrence U. Omoregbe, Director Brian Hanlon, & Director Richard Jackson (1490 Morris Rd SE, S03-A8QMU)

To the Freedom of Information Act Officers for the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE) and the Department of Buildings (DOB):

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am requesting copies of the following public records:

All internal emails, Microsoft Teams messages, chat logs, internal memos, notes, and corrective action directives sent between, involving, or copying Inspector Lawrence U. Omoregbe, DOB Director Brian Hanlon, and DOEE Director Richard Jackson regarding the site inspection, complaint investigation, and structural hazard reports for 1490 Morris Rd SE.

Timeframe:
This request covers all responsive records generated between March 15, 2026, and the date this request is processed.

Specific Scope of Records:
This request specifically includes, but is not limited to:
1. All internal correspondence discussing Inspector Omoregbe’s April 1, 2026 site visit and his report notation stating: "EMERGENCY DISPATCH REQUIRED: Imminent Catastrophic Tree Failure & Active Slope Collapse."
2. All communications, supervisory reviews, or directives discussing, modifying, or authorizing the recommendation to utilize "seeding" or "sodding" as a corrective measure for the structural slope failure at this address.
3. Any cross-agency communications between DOEE and DOB executive leadership regarding emergency ticket routing, jurisdictional responsibility, or media inquiries pertaining to this hazard.

Format & Timeline Requirement:
I strictly require all responsive files to be produced in their native digital format with all original metadata fully intact. Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c), I expect a full response within the statutory timeline of 15 business days.

Fee Waiver Request:
Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b) and 1 DCMR § 408.9, I am requesting a total waiver of all search and processing fees. This request is strictly in the public interest, as it directly concerns the physical safety of DC Prep students, families, and pedestrians navigating an active landslide along a public school walking route, as well as the preservation of a protected community canopy asset.

Please note that this request is being submitted via MuckRock.com, where all agency communications, production files, and procedural timelines will be tracked and published.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

RE: Public Records Request of August 26, 2026, Reference # R013212-082626 Dear FRED GAMBLE, The District of Columbia received a public records request from you on August 26, 2026. Your request mentioned: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records: 

Subject: DOEE/DOB Internal Communications: Inspector Lawrence U. Omoregbe, Director Brian Hanlon, & Director Richard Jackson (1490 Morris Rd SE, S03-A8QMU) 

To the Freedom of Information Act Officers for the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE) and the Department of Buildings (DOB): 

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am requesting copies of the following public records: 

All internal emails, Microsoft Teams messages, chat logs, internal memos, notes, and corrective action directives sent between, involving, or copying Inspector Lawrence U. Omoregbe, DOB Director Brian Hanlon, and DOEE Director Richard Jackson regarding the site inspection, complaint investigation, and structural hazard reports for 1490 Morris Rd SE. 

Timeframe: 
This request covers all responsive records generated between March 15, 2026, and the date this request is processed. 

Specific Scope of Records: 
This request specifically includes, but is not limited to: 
1. All internal correspondence discussing Inspector Omoregbe’s April 1, 2026 site visit and his report notation stating: "EMERGENCY DISPATCH REQUIRED: Imminent Catastrophic Tree Failure & Active Slope Collapse." 
2. All communications, supervisory reviews, or directives discussing, modifying, or authorizing the recommendation to utilize "seeding" or "sodding" as a corrective measure for the structural slope failure at this address. 
3. Any cross-agency communications between DOEE and DOB executive leadership regarding emergency ticket routing, jurisdictional responsibility, or media inquiries pertaining to this hazard. 

Format & Timeline Requirement: 
I strictly require all responsive files to be produced in their native digital format with all original metadata fully intact. Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c), I expect a full response within the statutory timeline of 15 business days. 

Fee Waiver Request: 
Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b) and 1 DCMR § 408.9, I am requesting a total waiver of all search and processing fees. This request is strictly in the public interest, as it directly concerns the physical safety of DC Prep students, families, and pedestrians navigating an active landslide along a public school walking route, as well as the preservation of a protected community canopy asset. 

Please note that this request is being submitted via MuckRock.com, where all agency communications, production files, and procedural timelines will be tracked and published. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Haunani-Kay Trask (October 3, 1949 – July 3, 2021)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into Professor Haunani-Kay Trask (October 3, 1949 – July 3, 2021). Her death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find her New York Times obituary at the following link: https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/09/us/haunani-kay-trask-dead.html

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Denton Flock Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Related to automated license plate reader (ALPR) or "Flock Safety" camera systems operated by or in partnership with the City:

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, or other instruments between the City of Denton and Flock Safety, Inc., or any related entity, including any amendments or renewals. (No date restriction.)

All invoices, payment records, and purchase orders related to Flock Safety equipment, software, or services. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All data retention policies governing footage, license plate reads, or associated metadata collected by Flock cameras. (No date restriction.)

All written policies, procedures, or general orders governing officer access to, and use of, Flock camera data. (No date restriction.)

All records reflecting the total number of Flock cameras deployed, their locations, and dates of installation. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All records of third-party data sharing, including but not limited to agreements or logs of data shared with other law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, or private parties. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All audit logs, access logs, or query logs reflecting searches of Flock camera data by City employees or contractors. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

All records reflecting complaints, grievances, or legal challenges related to the Flock camera program. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All communications, including email and internal messaging platform records, between City employees and Flock Safety, Inc. representatives regarding the procurement, deployment, expansion, or renewal of the program. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

Any privacy impact assessments, legal reviews, or internal memoranda regarding the program's compliance with Texas law. (No date restriction.)

If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please identify each withheld document by description, date, author, and recipient in a detailed withholding log, and specify the statutory exception claimed for each.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nayab Warach

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FY2024 prisoner operations details
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

(1) any record(s) detailing the average daily population of all individuals remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service in FY 2025 (or most recent fiscal year for which records are available), disaggregated or broken down by:
(a) sex; 
(b) most serious offense or charge (if that is not possible, then by offense category, i.e. violent, property, drugs, other new offense, weapons, immigration, supervision, material witness, etc.); 
(c) case status (i.e., convicted or unconvicted, or sentenced or unsentenced); 
(d) both sex and most serious offense (or if that is not possible, then by offense category) – i.e., the number of females in custody for each offense type and the number of males in custody for each offense type;
(e) both sex and case status (convicted or unconvicted, or sentenced or unsentenced) – i.e. the number of females in custody who are sentenced versus unsentenced and the number of males in custody who are sentenced versus unsentenced; and
(f) type of facility (i.e., state correctional facility, local correctional facility, privately owned or operated facilities, Federal Bureau of Prisons facilities, hospitals, or other).

If records are unavailable for the average daily population, records reporting the same information for any single day after January 1, 2024 (or the most recent day for which records are available) would be acceptable. Similarly, I would prefer records that contain this information reported as counts (totals), but if such records are unavailable, records reporting the same information by percent (percent of total) would be acceptable. I would also prefer the information be sent via email in PDF format, but would accept other electronic formats. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

I agree to pay any reasonable copying and postage fees of not more than $25. If the cost would be greater than this amount, please notify me. Please provide a receipt indicating the charges for each document. 

If you choose to deny this request, please provide a written explanation for the denial, including a reference to the specific statutory exemption(s) upon which you rely. Also, please provide all segregable portions of otherwise exempt material.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Wendy Sawyer

communications.subject: Wisconsin Open Records Act Request: Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Department (Everest Metro Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31–19.39, I hereby request the following records.
Subject: All records held by the Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Department — including records created or maintained by the predecessor agencies, the Everest Metropolitan Police Department and the Rothschild Police Department — pertaining to Stephanie Ann Low (DOB 09/29/1988).
Stephanie Ann Low was a resident of the Marathon County area who was reported missing in approximately October 2010 and whose remains were recovered in September 2014. She was the decedent in Marathon County criminal case No. 2014CF000860.
Time Frame: January 1, 2000 through December 31, 2014.
Records Requested:
I request all records in which Stephanie Ann Low appears as a subject, victim, suspect, witness, complainant, caller, or person of interest, including but not limited to:

Incident reports and supplemental reports — All incident reports, offense reports, supplemental reports, follow-up reports, and field contact reports in which Stephanie Ann Low is named or referenced.
911 call recordings and dispatch records — All recordings of 911 or non-emergency calls placed by or about Stephanie Ann Low, and all Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) records for any call involving her name, her known addresses, or her known associates in connection with her.
Booking records, arrest records, and mugshots — All booking photographs, arrest reports, fingerprint records, and custody records for Stephanie Ann Low.
Audio and video recordings — All audio recordings, including recorded interviews, interrogations, phone calls, and voicemails involving Stephanie Ann Low. All video recordings, including interview room video, surveillance video obtained in any investigation involving her, and any other video in which she appears or is discussed.
Body-worn camera footage — All body-worn camera recordings from any officer contact with Stephanie Ann Low, or any call for service at which she was present or discussed.
Squad car dashcam video — All squad car video recordings from any traffic stop, call for service, or other police contact involving Stephanie Ann Low.
Detective and investigator reports — All detective notes, investigative reports, case chronologies, intelligence reports, and memoranda referencing Stephanie Ann Low, including any missing person investigation, drug investigation, or other inquiry in which she was involved.
Witness statements — All written or recorded statements from or about Stephanie Ann Low in any investigation.
Evidence and property records — All evidence collection logs, property receipts, and evidence disposition records for any items associated with Stephanie Ann Low.
Communications with other agencies — All correspondence, emails, reports, and memoranda exchanged between the department (or its predecessor agencies) and any other law enforcement agency, the Marathon County District Attorney's Office, or the Marathon County Medical Examiner's Office regarding Stephanie Ann Low.
Traffic citations and warnings — All traffic citations, written warnings, and related records issued to Stephanie Ann Low.
Missing person records — All records related to any missing person report filed for Stephanie Ann Low, including the initial report, follow-up investigation, and any agency communications about her disappearance.
Any other records — Any other records not covered above in which Stephanie Ann Low is named, referenced, or depicted.

Note Regarding Predecessor Agency Records:
I understand that the Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Department was established on May 1, 2024, by merger of the Everest Metropolitan Police Department and the Rothschild Police Department. The records I am requesting would have been created by one or both predecessor agencies. As the successor department, the Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Department is the current custodian of those records. If any responsive records were transferred to another custodian or remain with a different entity, please advise so that I may direct a separate request accordingly.
Format and Fees:
I request that responsive records be provided electronically by email attachment or download link where possible. For audio and video files, USB flash drive or other electronic media is acceptable. If the total cost of fulfilling this request will exceed $50, please notify me in advance with an itemized estimate before proceeding.
This request is not made for commercial purposes. The records will be made available to the general public.
If any portion of this request requires further clarification to locate responsive records, please contact me before closing or denying any portion so that I may narrow or redirect as needed.
Thank you for your anticipated cooperation. I look forward to your response as soon as practicable and without delay as required by Wis. Stat. § 19.35(4)(a).
Sincerely,
Emma

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Emma

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide copies of the following records from January 1, 2024, to the date of this request, unless a different timeframe is specified below:

I. Contracts, Funding, and Acquisition
Please provide documents for Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 from the period between the inception of the agency's relationship with Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety) and the present.
1. All contracts, licensing agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) subscriptions, Master Services Agreements (MSA), and Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) between the San Bruno Police Department (or the City of San Bruno acting on its behalf) and Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety).
2. Any amendments, renewals, extensions, or change orders to the agreements described in Item 1.
3. All purchase orders, invoices, and records of payments made to Flock Safety.
4. Records identifying the specific funding sources used for these systems (e.g., General Fund, asset forfeiture funds, state/federal grants, or private donations).
5. All internal memos, proposals, or staff reports discussing the acquisition, approval, placement, or pilot programs for Flock ALPR cameras.

II. Policy, Privacy, and Governance
6. The current ALPR Usage and Privacy Policy, as required by California Civil Code § 1798.90.51, including data retention schedules and access protocols.
7. Annual ALPR audit reports required by Civil Code § 1798.90.53.
8. Training materials, policies, or directives provided to sworn and civilian personnel regarding authorized use of the Flock system.
9. Any Surveillance Use Policies, Anticipated Surveillance Impact Reports, or Privacy Impact Assessments related to ALPR technology generally or Flock Safety specifically.
10. The San Bruno Police Department's records about agendas, minutes, or logs of meetings regarding the contracting, implementation, or security of Flock Safety cameras.
11. Documentation regarding public notification of surveillance, including signage standards, maps provided to the public, or press releases.
12. Any complaints or grievances received from the public regarding ALPR camera placement or data use.

III. Operational and Technical Data
13. A list of all current and planned locations of Flock Safety ALPR cameras deployed by the San Bruno Police Department (including those in unincorporated areas and contract cities), including: coordinates or intersection descriptions, installation dates, the specific purpose for each location (e.g., traffic monitoring, crime prevention), camera model numbers/hardware specifications.
14. The names and titles of the specific System Administrators or managers responsible for the oversight of the Flock Safety system (e.g., Professional Services Division Commander).

IV. Usage Data, Sharing, and Audits
15. The total number of license plates scanned (read) by the San Bruno Police Department's Flock cameras, aggregated by month.
16. All existing audit or access logs generated by the Flock Safety system documenting queries/searches conducted by agency personnel. I request that personally identifiable information of non-employee subjects be redacted rather than the records withheld. Please include: date and time of search, reason for search (as entered into the system audit trail), and the agency or unit of the officer conducting the search.
17. Records regarding the sharing of ALPR data with the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center (NCRIC), including but not limited to: 
- Any MOUs, data-sharing agreements, or network-participation terms governing the transmission of the San Bruno Police Department's ALPR data to NCRIC; 
- Records describing the technical mechanism by which data is shared (e.g., automatic real-time feed, batch upload, or query-based access);
- Any policies, directives, or written guidance governing what restrictions, if any, the San Bruno Police Department places on NCRIC's downstream use or further dissemination of San Bruno Police Department-origin ALPR data;
- Records of any requests received from NCRIC (or through NCRIC from other agencies) to query or obtain San Bruno Police Department ALPR data, and the San Bruno Police Department's responses to such requests.
18. A list of all "hot lists" (e.g., stolen vehicles, Amber alerts) or custom "hot lists" currently integrated into the San Bruno Police Department Flock system.
19. A list of all outside agencies (local, state, and federal) that the San Bruno Police Department shares Flock data with, and a list of all outside agencies from whom the San Bruno Police Department receives Flock data, including but not limited to access provided through Flock Safety's real-time network sharing features (e.g., the platform previously known as TALON), and any data-sharing agreements, MOUs, or network participation terms governing such access.
20. Any statistical reports or evaluations generated by the department or Flock Safety regarding the efficacy of the system (e.g., number of vehicles recovered, arrests made attributable to ALPR hits).
21. Records of any unauthorized access, data breaches, or security incidents involving ALPR data.

V. Communication
22. All written communications (emails and attachments) between San Bruno Police Department employees and representatives of Flock Safety (email domain @flocksafety.com), excluding routine IT troubleshooting tickets.
23. All written communications with other law enforcement agencies or federal partners regarding requests to access or share San Bruno Police Department Flock data.

If you determine that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, please redact only those portions and provide the remainder of the record. For any redaction or denial, please cite the specific legal exemption justifying the withholding, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.

Given that this request is made in the public interest by a student journalist writing for Scot Scoop, I respectfully request a waiver or reduction of any fees associated with this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Maximus Kwan

The City received your Public Records Act (PRA) request via email on February 17, 2026, requesting that the City produce:

I. Contracts, Funding, and Acquisition

2. Any amendments, renewals, extensions, or change orders to the agreements described in Item 1.


3. All purchase orders, invoices, and records of payments made to Flock Safety.


4. Records identifying the specific funding sources used for these systems (e.g., General Fund, asset forfeiture funds, state/federal grants, or private donations).


5. All internal memos, proposals, or staff reports discussing the acquisition, approval, placement, or pilot programs for Flock ALPR cameras.

City Response:  The City has no responsive records to this request.



II. Policy, Privacy, and Governance


6. The current ALPR Usage and Privacy Policy, as required by California Civil Code § 1798.90.51, including data retention schedules and access protocols.
City Response: Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) Automated-License-Plate-Readers-Policy-PDF<https://www.sanbruno.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/1315/Automated-License-Plate-Readers-Policy-PDF?bidId=>



7. Annual ALPR audit reports required by Civil Code § 1798.90.53.
City Response: The Department conducts periodic audits of the ALPR system, including annual reviews, to ensure compliance with applicable law and Department policy; however, the Department has no responsive records for a standalone annual audit report. A PDF reflecting an additional audit conducted in January 2026, following the identification of changes to system settings was disclosed on April 13, 2026.



8. Training materials, policies, or directives provided to sworn and civilian personnel regarding authorized use of the Flock system.

9. Any Surveillance Use Policies, Anticipated Surveillance Impact Reports, or Privacy Impact Assessments related to ALPR technology generally or Flock Safety specifically.

City Response: https://www.sanbruno.ca.gov/530/Police-Transparency ;  https://transparency.flocksafety.com/san-bruno-ca-pd

10. The San Bruno Police Department's records about agendas, minutes, or logs of meetings regarding the contracting, implementation, or security of Flock Safety cameras.


11. Documentation regarding public notification of surveillance, including signage standards, maps provided to the public, or press releases.


12. Any complaints or grievances received from the public regarding ALPR camera placement or data use.

Montgomery, 205 Cal.App.3d 1011 (1988).

                                Captain Brent Schimek

                                Captain Jeremy Brandenburg

                                Chief Matthew Lethin

                                Lieutenant Michael Blundell

                                Lieutenant Shawn Greathouse

15. The total number of license plates scanned (read) by the San Bruno Police Department's Flock cameras, aggregated by month.

City Response:  PDF previously produced on April 13, 2026

16. All existing audit or access logs generated by the Flock Safety system documenting queries/searches conducted by agency personnel. - Records of any requests received from NCRIC (or through NCRIC from other agencies) to query or obtain San Bruno Police Department ALPR data, and the San Bruno Police Department's responses to such requests.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov.

FOIPA:

FOIPA
