The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 138 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 571 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,289 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 1,649 days for processing.

communications.communication:
Dear J Ader:

You requested a status update on *RD 64263*, a request our office received 
on July 13, 2020 and to which we initially replied on August 28, 2020. The 
request was assigned to our Tier 1 processing queue for review.

To give you an indication of our existing backlog for cases in Tier 1, 
there are approximately 816 cases ahead of yours. Unfortunately, the 
COVID-19 pandemic has created many unprecedented challenges in our work. 
The majority of the records that our customers request require our staff to 
be on-site to search for and review microfilm, microfiche, or original 
textual records. Staffing levels on-site have been severely limited with 
long periods where our facility was closed. Even as we expand our 
reopening, operations may be temporarily curtailed due to limited staffing 
and/or deteriorating local health conditions.

Our small staff has and will continue to work diligently to process each 
request as quickly as possible.

Please note, we will not respond to status update requests more than once 
every six months.

To notify this office of a change in your contact information or to track 
the status of your request, please telephone 301-837-3190 or e-mail 
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov. If you have specific questions regarding the 
subject of your request, please contact Stephanie Coon directly at 
stephanie.coon@nara.gov or 301-837-1604. All communications concerning this 
request should reference your case tracking number *RD* *64263*.

Sincerely,

Ashney Randle
Government Information Specialist
Special Access & FOIA Program (RF)
National Archives at College Park

communications.subject: National Archives FOIA RD 64263
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader,

I am writing in further response to your Freedom of Information Act request
of July 13, 2020 for records in the custody of the National Archives and
Records Administration. Your request for FBI case files 100-BS-30168 and
100-HQ-415677 on Abraham Maslow was received in this office on August 24,
2020 and assigned FOIA tracking number RD 64263.

Your request is nearing the front of our processing queue. Before we begin
processing your request, we want to verify your current contact information
and confirm that you are still interested in the records.

You may contact us by email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov. If we do not
hear from you within 90 calendar days from the date of this letter, your
FOIA request will be administratively closed.

If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by
regular U.S. mail or by e-mail. By filing an appeal, you preserve your
rights under the Freedom of Information Act and present the deciding agency
with an opportunity to review your request and reconsider its decision. If
you submit your appeal by regular mail, it should be addressed to the
Deputy Archivist of the United States (ND), National Archives and Records
Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road, Room 4200, College Park, Maryland
20740-6001. Both the letter and envelope should be clearly marked “FOIA
Appeal.” If you submit your appeal by email, please send it to foia@nara.gov,
addressed to the Deputy Archivist, with the words “FOIA Appeal” in the
subject line. If you exercise your right to appeal, please explain why you
believe this response does not meet the requirements of the Freedom of
Information Act. All communications concerning this request should
reference your FOIA tracking number.

If you would like the opportunity to discuss my response and attempt to
resolve your dispute without initiating the appeals process, you may
contact our FOIA Public Liaison for assistance:

Accessioned Executive Branch Records – Washington, DC Area

FOIA Requester Service Center: 301-837-3190

FOIA Public Liaison: Rebecca Calcagno

8601 Adelphi Road, Room 5500

College Park, MD 20740-6001

301-837-3190

You may also contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS),
the Federal FOIA Ombudsman’s office, for assistance. OGIS offers mediation
services to help resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal
agencies. The contact information for OGIS is:

Office of Government Information Services

College Park, MD 20740-6001

https://www.archives.gov/ogis

Sincerely,

Laurel Macondray

Archivist

College Park, MD 20740-6001

communications.subject: Your National Archives FOIA Request RD 64263
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader,

I completed processing the records you requested from the National Archives
and Records Administration under Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) tracking
number RD 64263.

You requested access to FBI case files 100-BS-30168 and 100-HQ-415677 on
Abraham Harold Maslow.

I completed a line-by-line review of the records you requested. Please be
advised, I have considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing
records and applying FOIA exemptions for this request. Information was
released to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of my review:


Records Requested Total Pages Pages Released in Full Pages Released in
Part Pages
Withheld in Full
100-BS-30168 53 41 12 0
100-HQ-415677 38 29 9 0
Total: 91 70 21 0

I withheld information protected under section (b) of the FOIA (5 U.S.C.
552). The specific reasons for the denials are:

TYPE OF INFORMATION WITHHELD

FOIA EXEMPTION or STATUTE

classified national security information

(b)(1)

information exempted from disclosure by statute

the statute in support of this (b)(3) withholding is 50 USC 3024 (i)(1),
which protects sensitive intelligence sources and methods

(b)(3)

identities of confidential sources

(b)(7)(D)


You or your designated representative may view the files at the National
Archives at College Park, Maryland. We require at least one week advance
notice to prepare for your visit and ask that you email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov with your FOIA tracking number (RD 64263) and
the date you plan to visit. Please monitor our web page
https://www.archives.gov/college-park for details and updates, as the
operating status for the facility could change, affecting opening hours for
the research rooms.


If you cannot visit our College Park facility, you may order a digital or
paper reproduction copy of the files at the cost of 80 cents per page. To
place a reproduction order, please forward this response to our office
email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. A
mailing/billing address is required to generate a price quote, so please
include that information with your reproduction request.


It is possible the fees to hire a researcher may be less than the
reproduction fees. If you are unable to visit and you wish to hire a
researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher
can be found at this link: https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help. The
National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

- All contracts, licenses, MOUs, MOAs, data agreements, letters of intent, State of Work documents, Scope of Work documents, and other agreement documents with Axon that were active any time between 1/1/2023 and 9/1/2026.

- All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to Axon dated between 1/1/2023 and 9/1/2026. Responsive materials include all invoices, bills, receipts, check stubs, or any other records, including those possessed in an electronic format.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

e

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to Vancouver Public Schools, its legal counsel, its board of directors, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, voucher approvals, board warrant registry items, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee, specifically including but not limited to the $9,000.00 check/warrant processed on or around March 10, 2026 under Account Code 10 E 530 9700.
3. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 4, 2022, through June 30, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks, settlement agreements, and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:
The District is advised that, per Washington law (Progressive Animal Welfare Soc. v. University of Wash.), attorney billing records for public payment are subject to disclosure. Only specific, narrow redactions (e.g., student names under FERPA) are permitted, as blanket privilege claims are invalid under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:
A response is expected within five business days as per RCW 42.56.520. The records, requested for non-commercial purposes, should be provided electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #R001116-080326
communications.communication:
Dear Jen Anderson,

Thank you for the general ledger entries provided on August 31, 2026. While the District has provided basic accounting records proving Check No. 415420 was processed, the response remains non-compliant with the full scope of the request under the Washington Public Records Act (PRA). I object to the administrative closure of this request based on the following deficiencies:

1. Item 1 (Line-Item Billing Sheets): Page 19 contains only a flat summary sheet referencing a block of 30.0 hours. Under Progressive Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) v. University of Washington, 125 Wash. 2d 243 (1994), attorney billing sheets and time blocks documenting public expenditures are public records subject to disclosure. Please produce the actual itemized time logs, dates, and detailed line-item billing entries submitted by McMinimee Law to justify the $10,500 total expenditure.

2. Item 2 (Over-Redaction of Settlement Agreement): Pages 8, 9, and 10 of the produced settlement contract are entirely blacked out. Under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co., 162 Wash. 2d 716 (2007) and RCW 42.56.210(1), blanket page-level withholdings are structurally unlawful. While the District must redact specific student-identifiable elements protected by FERPA, it is legally required to segment the record, leaving the systemic contractual terms, general operational agreements, and non-identifiable text fully visible. 

Please provide a revised, properly parsed production of the settlement agreement and the missing detailed time logs to satisfy this request.

Respectfully Submitted in the Public Interest,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: Fwd: FOIA Request Deletion: NARA-NGC-2020-000447
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Ader:

Thank you for submitting your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to
the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), via the
*FOIAOnline* website.  We received your request on March 16, 2020.  Your
request concerns FBI files.

Our office uses the *FOIAonline* portal for FOIA and Privacy Act requests
for the National Archives and Records Administration's *operational* records
(records created by this agency).  Your *FOIAOnline *request is for records
that may be *archival* records (records created by or originated in a
different agency but that may have been transferred to the legal custody of
NARA), to which access is restricted. Therefore, we have forwarded it to
our *Office of Research Services, Special Access and FOIA* (RF) staff who
handle FOIA requests for such archival records.

Since *Research Services* does not process FOIA requests through
*FOIAOnline*, we removed your request from the *FOIAOnline* website.  *Special
Access *staff will assign you a new tracking number, and respond directly
to you. In the future, if you need to follow up with that office directly,
please contact them at the address below, or electronically via email.

The National Archives and Records Administration
Special Access and FOIA Staff (RF)
8601 Adelphi Road, Room 5500
College Park, MD 20740

By phone: 301-837-3190
By fax: 301-837-1864
By email: specialaccess_foia@nara.gov

For your reference, a copy of your request with one attachment is below.

Please visit our website at www.archives.gov/foia for further information
about submitting a FOIA request to NARA.  On our main website,
www.archives.gov, you can learn more about the resources we offer to the
public, and you can access our online catalog.

Thank you for contacting the National Archives.

Sincerely,
Susan Gillett
Government Information Specialist
Office of General Counsel
National Archives and Records Administration
College Park, MD 20740-6001
301-837-3409
susan.gillett@nara.gov

Because I have determined that FBI case file number 100-HQ-454082 ends with
serial number 2, I am denying *only* this portion of your request on
procedural grounds. However, if you believe that 100-HQ-454082 is
responsive to your request, please contact me directly at
christopher.abraham@nara.gov or 301-837-2958 within ninety (90) calendar
days from the date of this letter. If we do not hear from you within ninety
(90) calendar days, we will administratively close* only *the portion of
your case relating to 100-HQ-454082.



All of the remaining materials require screening for categories of
information exempted from disclosure under the terms of the FOIA, prior to
public release. In particular, there are documents that may be redacted to
protect the identities of confidential sources, including FBI informant
codes and informant file numbers.



Collectively, the responsive materials in your request amount to
approximately 235 pages. Requests for FBI case files that do not exceed 700
pages are assigned to our first-tier processing queue. Taking into
consideration our existing backlog, the estimated time required to complete
the processing of your request is approximately 30 months from the date of
this letter.



Please note that once we have notified you that review is complete, you may
either visit our College Park, MD facility to view the file at no cost or
order a reproduction. You may order a reproduction copy at the cost of
$0.80 per page by contacting our office to place an order. We estimate that
the cost of a reproduction will be $188.00.

communications.subject: Re: FOIA Case No. RD 64052 re Multiple FBI Records Concerning Murray Bookchin
communications.communication:
Dear Sir -



I contacted the FBI on your behalf concerning the outstanding issues
on 62-HQ-117964 and 100-HQ-454082 . As I indicated in my email of March
23rd, I was unable to locate 62-HQ-117964 in its entirety and unable to
locate 100-HQ-454082 serials 4-6 and 24 during the allotted search time. As
a final search tactic, I contacted FBI on your behalf about these two
issues and have just today received a response.


*62-HQ-117964* - FBI indicates it still has 62-HQ-117964  in its
possession. Therefore, I recommend that you contact the FBI directly (
https://www.fbi.gov/services/records-management/foipa) if you wish to
request it.




*100-HQ-454082 serials 4-6 and 24* - FBI concurs with the National Archives
that the case was transferred here, but cannot give an accounting of the
serial numbers within it. As you will recall from my email of the 23rd, we
only have serials 1 and 2 for this case file. Therefore, this portion of
your request remains denied on procedural grounds as previously outlined.
Regardless,if you believe that this file is still responsive to your
request, please see the instructions included in my email of the 23rd to
keep it an active portion of the request.


Sincerely,


*Chris Abraham*
Archivist
Special Access and FOIA Branch (RF)
301.837.2958
www.archives.gov/research/foia/

communications.communication:
February 19, 2026

Dear Mr. Ader,

I am writing in further response to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
request RD 64052 for records in the custody of the National Archives and
Records Administration.

Some of the records you requested have been reviewed for another requester
(RD 61316). Please be advised, we have considered the foreseeable harm
standard when reviewing records and applying FOIA exemptions for this
request. Information was released to the greatest extent possible. Below is
a summary of our review:

You requested access to  FBI case file numbers: 100-HQ-454549 Serial 4 and
Serial 6, 100-HQ-455596, 100-HQ-456482 Serial 9, 100-HQ-461197 Serials 2
and 13, 100-NY-166899, 100-BS-47199 Serial 1, and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435.
These files have been reviewed for another requestor.

You requested 88-HQ-49004 serials 76, 77, 89, 90, 91, 97, 113, 118, 130,
145, 166, 186 which are still in the processing queue.

You requested 100-BS-46975, currently only Serial 10 of 100-BS-46975 has
been reviewed for another requestor, the remaining file is still in the
queue.

I completed a line-by-line review of the records you requested. Please be
advised, I have considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing
records and applying FOIA exemptions for this request. Information was
released to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of my review:

Part Pages
Withheld in Full

100-NY-166899 126 108 18 0

100-BS-47199 Serial 1 2 1 1 0
100-AL-21998 Serial 435 4 4 0 0

I withheld information protected under section (b) of the FOIA (5 U.S.C.
552). The specific reasons for the denials are:

TYPE OF INFORMATION WITHHELD

FOIA EXEMPTION or STATUTE

classified national security information

(b)(1)

privileged or confidential trade secrets and commercial or financial
information

(b)(4)

personal privacy of living individuals

(b)(6)

identities of confidential sources

(b)(7)(D)

You or your designated representative may view the file(s) at the National
Archives at College Park, Maryland. We require at least one week advance
notice to prepare for your visit and ask that you email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov with the FOIA tracking number of the previous
requestor (RD 61316) as well as your FOIA tracking number (RD 64052) and
the date you plan to visit. Please monitor our web page
https://www.archives.gov/college-park for details and updates, as the
operating status for the facility could change, affecting opening hours for
the research rooms.

If you cannot visit our College Park facility, you may order a digital or
paper reproduction copy of the file(s) at the cost of 80 cents per page. To
place a reproduction order, please forward this response to our office
email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. A
mailing/billing address is required to generate a price quote, so please
include that information with your reproduction request.


It is possible the fees to hire a researcher may be less than the
reproduction fees. If you are unable to visit and you wish to hire a
researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher
can be found at this link: https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help. The
National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list

If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by
regular U.S. mail or by email. By filing an appeal, you preserve your
rights under the Freedom of Information Act and present the deciding agency
with an opportunity to review your request and reconsider its decision. If
you submit your appeal by regular mail, it should be addressed to the
Deputy Archivist of the United States (ND), National Archives and Records
Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road, Room 4200, College Park, Maryland
20740-6001. Both the letter and envelope should be clearly marked “FOIA
Appeal.” If you submit your appeal by email, please send it to foia@nara.gov,
addressed to the Deputy Archivist, with the words “FOIA Appeal” in the
subject line. If you exercise your right to appeal, please explain why you

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Complaints to Blue Ash (Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

On behalf of my client, Ohio Immigrant Alliance:

For the ICE Blue Ash Field Office, since 2020;

1. All closed JIC complaints or communications that were created; and,
2. Subsequent investigative reports.


I request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 CFR 5.5(e) and state under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746 that these records are a matter of widespread interest (federal enforcement of immigration laws and the conduct of ICE officials) and about which there exist serious questions of government wrongdoing and public safety. Moreover, my client, Ohio Immigrant Alliance disseminates information about immigration enforcement activities. See https://www.ohioimmigrant.org, especially the drop-down boxes on the home page titled "News" and "Multimedia." There is an urgent need to inform the public about the extent to which complaints related to this office have been substantiated and the corrective measures were recommended.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Lara S Nochomovitz

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

A list of anyone that was arrested for lying on their job application to the Bruceville-Eddy Police Department in the last 5 years.  I understand that the Open Records Act does not require a city to create documents that do not exist.  So if this request does not produce a list, I would like to request the "Form 6" or "warrant" for any individual that has been charged with tampering with a government document, or any related charge so far as their application for employment within the agency. Jason Garcia would be a start, but it is far from the only record I am requesting.

To preclude a request to the AG Office, I am NOT requesting any personal identifying information that would ordinarily be covered by the Open Records Act.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Bernadette Feazell

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: City of Oakland March 4 Rejection Letters
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. March 2026 claim rejection letters. All letters, notices, or other written communications issued by or on behalf of the City of Oakland during the period March 1, 2026 through March 31, 2026, inclusive, that reject, deny, return as untimely, return as insufficient, or otherwise dispose of a claim for money or damages presented to the City under the Government Claims Act (Gov. Code, § 900 et seq.). This includes documents titled "Notice of Rejection," "Notice of Insufficiency," "Notice of Untimeliness," "Notice of Return of Claim," and any equivalent form letter, regardless of the title used.

2. The March 4, 2026 letters specifically. Without limiting Item 1, all such letters issued on or about March 4, 2026 on claims arising out of the City's closure of, and enforcement action at, the E. 12th Street median encampment.

3. Transmittal records. For each letter responsive to Items 1 and 2, the transmittal record showing the date the letter was mailed, emailed, or otherwise served and the address or addresses to which it was sent (including cover letters, mailing logs, proof-of-service forms, certified mail receipts, or email transmittal messages).

4. Claim log or register. Any claim log, register, spreadsheet, database export, or tracking report identifying claims presented to the City that were rejected, returned, or otherwise disposed of in March 2026, showing at minimum the claim number, claimant name, date of claim, date of disposition, and disposition type. A report or export generated from the City's existing claims-tracking system is acceptable and is not the creation of a new record where the system can produce it in the ordinary course.

5. Council or delegated-authority action. Any City Council agenda item, resolution, staff report, or delegated-authority determination approving or authorizing the rejection of the claims described in Items 1 and 2.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

In response to your request for items 3 through 4, attached is the City’s contract with Flock Safety. I have also included a link to the Blue Springs Police Department’s Flock Safety Transparency Portal:
https://transparency.flocksafety.com/blue-springs-mo-pd

The transparency portal provides access to our applicable policy and identifies the agencies or entities with which data may be shared. There are no individual data-sharing agreements between agencies. Data sharing is elective and is determined by each agency utilizing the Flock Safety system.
Additional Police Department policies and information are available through the City of Blue Springs website.
Regarding Questions 1 and 2, Missouri law requires a governmental body to produce existing public records; however, it does not require a governmental body to create a new record or compile information that does not already exist in response to a records request. See Weeks v. St. Louis County, 696 S.W.3d 333 (Mo. banc 2024), and Jones v. Jackson County Circuit Court, 162 S.W.3d 53, 60 (Mo. App. W.D. 2005). Answering questions 1 and 2 would create a new record as described above.

communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under the North Carolina Public Records Law, N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-1 et seq., I request the following existing record: The daily jail booking log (booking register / arrest blotter) for all individuals booked into your facility from January 1, 2025 through the present. For each booking, I request the fields your booking system already records: (1) name of the individual booked; (2) date and time of booking; (3) the charge(s) and offense level; (4) bond amount and type, and the date any bond was posted; and (5) the date and manner of release from your custody. This is routine booking data maintained in your jail-management system in the ordinary course. I will accept it in whatever native electronic format your system exports (a spreadsheet or delimited file is ideal; I do not require a formatted report). As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if any fee is anticipated, please provide an itemized written estimate before incurring cost. Please preserve all responsive records pending completion.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein
